pr_title: CSS: Detect more WebKit styles erroneously reported as percentages
pr_body:
Ref 692f9d4db30c9c6c4f6bc76005cf153586202fa6
Fixes gh-3777

### Summary ###
We already caught Android 4.0 - 4.3 `getComputedStyle` reporting percentage values for margin properties, but the problem also affects other styles, and Safari and iOS.

issue_context.title: Safari and iOS fail bounded-style relative adjustment
issue_context.body:
### Description ###
Safari and iOS fail the new test added by 692f9d4db30c9c6c4f6bc76005cf153586202fa6.

### Link to test case ###
http://swarm.jquery.org/job/6075

review_comments: So is it okay that `rboxStyle` now catches properties like `borderLeftWidth`? Our CSS unit tests don't seem to do much with the `border*Width` properties so I'm just wondering what effect we'll have in going through this path.

It's fine because the swap logic only kicks in when gCS returns a non-px unitful value. And even if that does happen, the only consequence is taking a slower path (requiring layout calculation) to get pixels.
Huh. How did we end up with a regex here in the first place?
The regex also matched margin-top, margin-right, etc.
